s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules and lymphoid infiltrate
salient_findings: Erythematous papules with crusts and excoriations on the trunk and upper extremities
Scales and fissures on the lower lip with sparing of the surrounding skin
key_facts: Female patient in her early 40s
No other medical history
Topical corticosteroids ineffective in controlling symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, crusts, and excoriations
Scales and fissures on the lower lip
Normal blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement
Normal urine porphyrin analysis
Skin biopsy showed spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis
Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis
CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells in the germinal center
Phototest with solar simulator showed delayed erythema to UV-A

shortlist.label: mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: lymphoid infiltrate and CD20 positive cells in skin biopsy

shortlist.label: contact dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: delayed erythema to UV-A in phototest

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of generalized pruritus, erythematous papules, and excoriations, along with the ineffectiveness of topical corticosteroids, is consistent with atopic dermatitis. The skin biopsy findings of spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: The presence of CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells in the germinal center is not typical for mycosis fungoides, which usually shows a predominance of CD4 positive T-cells.

rejected.label: bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: The lack of blistering or bullae in the patient's presentation makes bullous pemphigoid less likely.

rejected.label: psoriasis
rejected.why: The absence of characteristic psoriatic plaques and the presence of spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis are not typical for psoriasis.

rejected.label: contact dermatitis
rejected.why: The generalized nature of the patient's symptoms and the lack of a clear contact allergen make contact dermatitis less likely.
